text: Water.
It is the foundation of life.
For thousands of years, our lakes have sustained entire ecosystems.
But beneath their still surfaces, something can change.
When water turns too acidic, the delicate conditions that life depends on can be threatened.
You cannot see it happen.
And restoring that balance, by hand, lake by lake, is not simple.
What if technology could work alongside nature, to help protect it?
This is where it begins.
A black box. A solar panel. A float.
No name. No logo.
Just an idea, built by hand, and tested in a backyard pool.
Then, it earned a name.
Alkalac.
It is a prototype. It has never touched a lake.
Not yet.
Imagine it here.
The design concept works like this.
Sunlight becomes power.
A sensor is designed to watch the water's acidity.
And when the balance slips, the concept is to release a measured dose of crushed limestone,
a mineral that can neutralise acidity, helping the water find its way back.
One day, there could be many.
Quiet machines, working together, watching over the water.
Because the future of our lakes should not be left to chance.
It should be built with intention.
With science. With engineering.
And with a responsibility to protect what sustains us.
Alkalac.
Technology in service of nature.
